## What to build

`ko build file.ko` emits a platform-native binary via Zig AOT, so `.ko` programs can be distributed and run without the `ko` interpreter. Loop optimizations are applied during build where eligible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ko build file.ko` produces an executable for the current OS/arch
- [ ] Produced binary runs the same `.ko` program as `ko run`
- [ ] Build applies Loop.cpp optimizations where applicable
- [ ] Build fails on unsupported features with clear diagnostics
- [ ] Build artifact is deterministic/repeatable
- [ ] Output path/name is configurable or predictable

## Blocked by

- #6: Lexer/AST Refactor + Bytecode VM
- #13: Loop Optimization Subsystem (shared lib)

## What to build

A GitHub-hosted flat-file registry (`ko-lang/registry`) with a JSON index, plus `ko install`, `ko list`, and `ko search` commands. Installation fetches a zip, compiles/links it, and registers the module scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Registry metadata is served from a GitHub repo with raw access
- [ ] `ko install <lib>` fetches library metadata and zip
- [ ] `ko install` compiles/links supported languages and registers scope
- [ ] `ko list` shows installed libraries
- [ ] `ko search <query>` searches registry metadata
- [ ] Failure paths purge downloaded artifacts and report clearly
- [ ] Versioning uses SemVer and writes `ko.lock`

## Blocked by

- #5: CLI Framework & `ko <file>` / `ko run <code>`
- #9: Plugin Loader + `Import` Subsystem (shared lib)
issues.title: 05: Registry Client + `ko install/list/search`

issues.body:
## What to build

`Loop.cpp` is compiled into a shared library (`libko_loop.so` / `.dylib` / `.dll`) and loaded through the same plugin contract as `Import`. The `Loop` keyword offloads hot loop execution to the C++ engine, enabling cache-line and CPU-register optimizations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Loop.cpp` builds as a shared library
- [ ] Zig loads `libko_loop.so` via the plugin loader
- [ ] `Loop` keyword hands iteration to the C++ engine
- [ ] Optimizations are active for eligible loops
- [ ] Missing plugin fails clearly
- [ ] Performance improves for long-running loops

## Blocked by

- #9: Plugin Loader + `Import` Subsystem (shared lib)

## What to build

Compiler diagnostics include file, line, and column; parse phase collects all errors before stopping; runtime errors include source context and a log output. Errors are declared clearly by the compiler, not buried in generic messages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parse error includes file, line, column, and message
- [ ] Multiple parse errors in one file are all reported
- [ ] Runtime error shows source context and log output
- [ ] Error format is stable enough for tooling/editor integration
- [ ] Existing Zig tests still pass

- #6: Lexer/AST Refactor + Bytecode VM

## What to build

An interactive `ko repl` mode with history and multi-line input, letting users evaluate `.ko` expressions and statements incrementally against the same VM/bytecode pipeline as script execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single-line statements evaluate immediately
- [ ] Multi-line input is supported for block/function definitions
- [ ] History navigation works within the session
- [ ] Errors show file/line context (`<input>` or `<repl>`)

- [ ] `ko repl` starts an interactive session

## What to build

Zig can dynamically load a shared library (`libko_import.so` / `.dylib` / `.dll`) that implements the `Import` subsystem. `Import.java` is compiled to this shared library and loaded on demand. Convention paths `libs/` (project) and `~/.ko/plugins/` (global) are scanned for plugins.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Zig loads a shared library via a defined C-ABI
- [ ] `Import` keyword in `.ko` triggers the plugin
- [ ] Plugin resolves module paths and registers scope
- [ ] Missing plugin fails with a clear error
- [ ] Convention paths `libs/` and `~/.ko/plugins/` are searched

## Blocked by

- #6: Lexer/AST Refactor + Bytecode VM

issues.body:
## What to build

Refactor `lexer.zig` and `ast.zig` into a clean shared representation, and implement a fast bytecode VM in `vm.zig` so `.ko` programs execute via compiled bytecode instead of AST walking. Existing Zig tests continue to pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Lexer and AST types are refactored without changing public behavior
- [ ] VM emits/executes bytecode for a representative `.ko` program
- [ ] `zig build test` passes
- [ ] Performance target: simple loop program executes measurably faster than AST-walk baseline

## Blocked by

- #5: CLI Framework & `ko <file>` / `ko run <code>`

## Implementation note

This is a wide refactor with blast radius across parser/VM/tests. Sequence as expand–contract:
1. Add new lexer/AST/bytecode forms beside existing ones
2. Migrate parser
3. Migrate VM
4. Remove old forms once nothing calls them
issues.title: 02: Lexer/AST Refactor + Bytecode VM
